addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content: 1 # [BUG] A quality/gear effect's bonus for Tests silently stops applying 2 3 **Describe the bug** 4 An Active Effect that's supposed to add a bonus to a character for certain Tests no longer does 5 anything. There's no error or warning anywhere — the effect is just quietly inert, and the roll 6 dialog never reflects it. 7 8 This particular effect is an older one: it was set up on this item a while ago, before a recent 9 system update, and hasn't been touched since. Whatever fixes it needs to apply automatically 10 wherever this shows up — however the old data happens to be stored, not just for this one example 11 — without disturbing anything else already configured on the same effect or interfering with how 12 the system brings other older content up to date. 13 14 **Screenshots** 15 16 17 18 The screenshot shows how this kind of effect is set up and what a correctly working one looks 19 like — the pictured effect's own stored values aren't necessarily the exact data that needs 20 fixing. 21 22 **Versions (please complete the following information):** 23 - FoundryVTT Version 13.351 24 - System Version 0.33.0 25

file.content: # [BUG] A quality/gear effect's bonus for Tests silently stops applying **Describe the bug** An Active Effect that's supposed to add a bonus to a character for certain Tests no longer does anything. There's no error or warning anywhere — the effect is just quietly inert, and the roll dialog never reflects it. This particular effect is an older one: it was set up on this item a while ago, before a recent system update, and hasn't been touched since. Whatever fixes it needs to apply automatically wherever this shows up — however the old data happens to be stored, not just for this one example — without disturbing anything else already configured on the same effect or interfering with how the system brings other older content up to date. **Screenshots** The screenshot shows how this kind of effect is set up and what a correctly working one looks like — the pictured effect's own stored values aren't necessarily the exact data that needs fixing. **Versions (please complete the following information):** - FoundryVTT Version 13.351 - System Version 0.33.0

20	modern data-key spelling, the word "migration", the effect's own configuration (which item, its
21	change mode, what it applies to), AND which specific test value the bonus targets -- it only
22	says "a bonus" stopped applying "for certain Tests" and that the effect predates a recent
23	update. The current TestData schema exposes exactly three ValueFieldType fields a Test-scoped
24	Custom effect could plausibly target (pool, threshold, limit); without the poster, nothing in
25	the bundle tells a solver WHICH of those three is the one silently failing, so a solver reasoning
26	from schema + text alone cannot determine where to point the fix. The poster is the ONLY place
27	that resolves this: it shows the Sneaking Test dialog's Pool not reflecting the Catlike effect's
28	bonus while a different item's bonus on Limit DOES apply -- singling out pool specifically -- and
29	it is also the ONLY place that shows WHICH effect/item is implicated (a "Catlike" quality's
30	Changes tab) and its concrete configuration (Custom mode, applied to a Test), which the agent
31	needs to actually find the responsible code path across two files rather than reason from the
32	bug title alone.
33	
34	Screenshot-accuracy caveat (read before assuming the image proves the legacy key): the
35	Attribute Key field visibly rendered in bug_screenshot_1.png reads `data.pool` (the MODERN
36	key), not `data.modifiers` (the legacy key this fix migrates). This is the genuine, correctly-
37	sourced GitHub attachment (asset id 89890be5-8e82-4aab-9faf-f9fed89e6d58 verified to match the
38	live issue), not a wrong/cropped/mismatched image -- but its visible content does not, by
39	itself, evidence the legacy-key mechanism the fix addresses (a `data.pool`-keyed effect would
40	not need migrating at all under this fix's logic). The poster's load-bearing contribution is
41	therefore narrower than "shows the bug": it localizes WHICH item/effect/field is involved (Custom
42	mode, applied to a Test, targeting pool specifically), not the historical key spelling itself.
43	That remaining fact -- the exact legacy string -- still has to come from general reasoning over
44	the current repo (the schema enumerates the only legitimate targets; anything else on a
45	test-scoped Custom effect is presumably stale and should normalize to the one the poster
46	identifies), not from the image's pixels or from instruction.md's text.
47	
48	Why the fix is non-trivial: SR5 renamed the SuccessTest data key that an `apply-to: test`
49	Active Effect change writes into from `data.modifiers` to `data.pool`, but shipped no migration
50	step rewriting the change key on effects authored (or imported) before that rename -- so any
51	such effect (the issue's own reproduction: an "apply-to test" Custom-mode change targeting
52	`data.modifiers`) silently stops granting its dice-pool bonus, with no error anywhere.
53	The task's fix.patch adds "Case B" logic to the migrator, generalized rather than a literal
54	`data.modifiers`/`data.modifiers.mod` string match: for a `test_all`/`test_item`-scoped effect,
55	any change key that is NOT one of the three fields the current test data schema actually
56	exposes (`data.pool`, `data.threshold`, `data.limit`) is normalized to `data.pool`, reached
57	through Migrator.migrate()'s existing, pre-existing entry point. This is a deliberate departure
58	from the real upstream PR's literal-string diff -- made because the exact legacy spelling is not
59	fairly derivable inside this task's sandbox (no network, `.git` stripped, and the string does not
60	appear anywhere in the checked-out tree), so pinning the reference fix and tests to that exact
61	string would test a fact nobody could legitimately reach. The whitelist-based version tests the
62	same underlying contract with a solvable path: read the current schema, recognize it's closed to
63	three fields, and normalize anything else. The scoping matters: only `test_all`/`test_item`-scoped
64	effects are rewritten (an actor- or item-targeting effect that happens to also use a
65	non-canonical key must be left alone), the three canonical fields are never rewritten (an
66	unrelated change key on the same effect must survive untouched -- `tests_overfit_*` scrutiny
67	already confirmed a synthetic, non-historical key must ALSO migrate, proving the fix isn't just
68	special-casing the two literal legacy strings), and the migration must compose correctly with the
69	surrounding version-migration chain (an older effect must still receive migrations from earlier,
70	unrelated VersionMigration subclasses already registered in Migrator.s_Versions).
71	
72	base_commit/fix_commit note: issues #1830 and #1831 were fixed by commits on a since-deleted
73	feature branch (taMiF/issue1831) that are NOT reachable via a plain `git clone` now that the
74	branch is gone -- confirmed empirically (`git clone` followed by `git checkout <that commit>`
75	fails with "fatal: unable to read tree", even though the same commit can still be fetched
76	individually by exact SHA via `git fetch origin <sha>`, which GitHub permits for a time after a
77	branch deletion but a plain clone never surfaces). The only reachable commit carrying this fix
78	is 2f4323f4d5158ab0b258804d8ebdaa97a27654db, the squash-merge of sibling PR #1835 (branch
79	taMiF/issue1832), whose own PR body says "Includes changes for PR #1834 in Migrator for 0.33.1,
80	that can be ignored here" -- i.e. even that PR's own author treated the Migrator/Version0_33_1
81	hunks as inherited baggage from the (separately authored) #1830/#1831 fix, not as #1832's own

1	FROM node:22-bookworm
2	
3	# System build deps: git (for repo init/apply), ca-certificates/curl for the clone.
4	RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
5	    git \
6	    ca-certificates \
7	    curl \
8	 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
9	
10	WORKDIR /app
11	
12	# Clone the SR5-FoundryVTT system at the base commit, then STRIP .git so the
13	# agent cannot inspect the fix PR or future history (anti-cheat). Re-init a
14	# single base commit with an immutable tag so `git apply` still works and the
15	# verifier can reset test files.
16	RUN git clone https://github.com/SR5-FoundryVTT/SR5-FoundryVTT /app \
17	 && git -C /app checkout 074121360c08d8ee9288d1c3ac9ce61bdad8545b \
18	 && rm -rf /app/.git \
19	 && git -C /app init -q \
20	 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
21	 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
22	 && git -C /app tag harbor_base
23	
24	# Install npm dependencies (includes the pinned TypeScript compiler used by the
25	# verifier's standalone test harness). --ignore-scripts skips postinstall hooks
26	# that may need a display or native build tooling neither the agent nor the
27	# verifier need here.

FROM node:22-bookworm

# System build deps: git (for repo init/apply), ca-certificates/curl for the clone.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Clone the SR5-FoundryVTT system at the base commit, then STRIP .git so the
# agent cannot inspect the fix PR or future history (anti-cheat). Re-init a
# single base commit with an immutable tag so `git apply` still works and the
# verifier can reset test files.
RUN git clone https://github.com/SR5-FoundryVTT/SR5-FoundryVTT /app \
 && git -C /app checkout 074121360c08d8ee9288d1c3ac9ce61bdad8545b \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Install npm dependencies (includes the pinned TypeScript compiler used by the
# verifier's standalone test harness). --ignore-scripts skips postinstall hooks
# that may need a display or native build tooling neither the agent nor the
# verifier need here.
RUN npm install --ignore-scripts

# Visual evidence, readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/.
# tests/ and solution/ are intentionally NOT copied into the image —
# the harness supplies them at verify time.
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]

#      legacy_test_modifier_migration_matches_full_applyto_and_key_matrix

#      unrelated_change_key_on_test_effect_is_left_alone
#      effect_already_at_current_system_version_is_not_touched_at_all

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Robustness + idempotency ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Restore every path that test.patch touches to the pristine harbor_base state
# BEFORE applying, so (a) agent edits to the test can't affect scoring and (b) the

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Reward verifier for SR5-FoundryVTT__SR5-FoundryVTT-1831-mm.
4	
5	Reads /logs/verifier/report.xml (JUnit XML written by test_migrator_test_modifier_key.mjs),
6	matches test results against config.json's f2p/p2p lists, and writes the reward to
7	/logs/verifier/reward.json (and reward.txt, which the sandbox teardown script and the
8	lighthouse UI read instead).
9	
10	Reward policy (binary -- there is no partial credit):
11	  1.0  - every f2p test passes AND every p2p test passes
12	  0.0  - otherwise (a partial f2p pass, a p2p regression -- e.g. the apply-to scoping was
13	         dropped, or the migration list lost one of its pre-existing entries -- or the
14	         suite failed to produce a report at all)
15	"""
16	import atexit
17	import json
18	import os
19	import re
20	import sys
21	import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
22	
23	CONF   = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
24	F2P    = CONF['f2p']
25	P2P    = CONF['p2p']
26	REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'
27	REWARD = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
28	REWARD_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'
29	
30	_canon = {}
31	
32	
33	def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
34	    """THE reward policy. BINARY -- there is no partial credit."""
35	    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
36	    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
37	    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
38	    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
39	    _canon.clear()
40	    _canon.update({
41	        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
42	        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
43	        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
44	        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
45	        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
46	    })
47	    return _canon["reward"]
48	
49	
50	@atexit.register
51	def _canon_flush():
52	    if not _canon:
53	        return
54	    try:
55	        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(REWARD_JSON), exist_ok=True)
56	        with open(REWARD_JSON, 'w') as fh:
57	            json.dump(_canon, fh, indent=2)
58	        with open(REWARD, 'w') as fh:
59	            fh.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
60	    except Exception as exc:
61	        print(f'WARNING: could not write {REWARD_JSON}: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
62	
63	
64	def rubric_verdict(argv):
65	    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`.
66	
67	    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail -- including the empty string test.sh
68	    passes when judge.py wrote no verdict -- means "not graded", which must never
69	    penalise the run.
70	    """
71	    if '--rubric' not in argv:
72	        return None
73	    i = argv.index('--rubric')
74	    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ''
75	    return value if value in ('pass', 'fail') else None
76	
77	
78	def load_results():
79	    """Return {test_name: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} parsed from JUnit XML."""
80	    results = {}
81	    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
82	        return results
83	    try:
84	        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
85	    except ET.ParseError as e:
86	        print(f'[verifier] XML parse error: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
87	        return results
88	    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
89	        name = tc.get('name', '')
90	        cls  = tc.get('classname', '')
91	        key  = f'{cls}::{name}' if cls else name
92	        tags = {c.tag for c in tc}
93	        if 'skipped' in tags:
94	            status = 'skip'
95	        elif tags & {'failure', 'error'}:
96	            status = 'fail'
97	        else:
98	            status = 'pass'
99	        results[key]  = status
100	        results[name] = status   # also index by bare name for easy matching
101	    return results
102	
103	
104	def match_idents(idents, results):
105	    """Match each configured identifier against reported test names.
106	
107	    Matching strategy (in order):
108	      1. Exact key match.
109	      2. Substring match (ident contained in a reported key).
110	      3. Regex search (re.escape of ident against reported keys).
111	    Returns {ident: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'|'missing'}.
112	    """
113	    out = {}
114	    for ident in idents:
115	        if ident in results:
116	            out[ident] = results[ident]
117	            continue
118	        hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if ident in k), None)
119	        if hit is not None:
120	            out[ident] = hit
121	            continue
122	        try:
123	            pat = re.compile(re.escape(ident))
124	            hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if pat.search(k)), None)
125	        except re.error:
126	            hit = None
127	        out[ident] = hit if hit is not None else 'missing'
128	    return out
129	
130	
131	def main():
132	    results = load_results()
133	    f2p_res = match_idents(F2P, results)
134	    p2p_res = match_idents(P2P, results)
135	
136	    f2p_pass   = [k for k, v in f2p_res.items() if v == 'pass']
137	    p2p_pass   = [k for k, v in p2p_res.items() if v == 'pass']
138	
139	    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P), len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),
140	                           rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))
141	
142	    print(json.dumps({
143	        'reward': reward,
144	        'f2p':    f2p_res,
145	        'p2p':    p2p_res,
146	        'f2p_pass_count': len(f2p_pass),
147	        'f2p_total':      len(F2P),
148	        'p2p_pass_count': len(p2p_pass),
149	        'p2p_total':      len(P2P),
150	    }, indent=2))
151	
152	
153	if __name__ == '__main__':
154	    main()

"""
Reward verifier for SR5-FoundryVTT__SR5-FoundryVTT-1831-mm.

Reads /logs/verifier/report.xml (JUnit XML written by test_migrator_test_modifier_key.mjs),
matches test results against config.json's f2p/p2p lists, and writes the reward to
/logs/verifier/reward.json (and reward.txt, which the sandbox teardown script and the
lighthouse UI read instead).

Reward policy (binary -- there is no partial credit):
  1.0  - every f2p test passes AND every p2p test passes
  0.0  - otherwise (a partial f2p pass, a p2p regression -- e.g. the apply-to scoping was
         dropped, or the migration list lost one of its pre-existing entries -- or the
         suite failed to produce a report at all)
"""
import atexit
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF   = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P    = CONF['f2p']
P2P    = CONF['p2p']
REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'
REWARD = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
REWARD_JSON = '/logs/verifier/reward.json'

_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy. BINARY -- there is no partial credit."""
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon["reward"]


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(REWARD_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(REWARD_JSON, 'w') as fh:
            json.dump(_canon, fh, indent=2)
        with open(REWARD, 'w') as fh:
            fh.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f'WARNING: could not write {REWARD_JSON}: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`.

    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail -- including the empty string test.sh
    passes when judge.py wrote no verdict -- means "not graded", which must never
    penalise the run.
    """
    if '--rubric' not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index('--rubric')
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ''
    return value if value in ('pass', 'fail') else None


def load_results():
    """Return {test_name: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} parsed from JUnit XML."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as e:
        print(f'[verifier] XML parse error: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
        name = tc.get('name', '')
        cls  = tc.get('classname', '')
        key  = f'{cls}::{name}' if cls else name
        tags = {c.tag for c in tc}
        if 'skipped' in tags:
            status = 'skip'
        elif tags & {'failure', 'error'}:
            status = 'fail'
        else:
            status = 'pass'
        results[key]  = status
        results[name] = status   # also index by bare name for easy matching
    return results


def match_idents(idents, results):
    """Match each configured identifier against reported test names.

    Matching strategy (in order):
      1. Exact key match.
      2. Substring match (ident contained in a reported key).
      3. Regex search (re.escape of ident against reported keys).
    Returns {ident: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'|'missing'}.
    """
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        if ident in results:
            out[ident] = results[ident]
            continue
        hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if ident in k), None)
        if hit is not None:
            out[ident] = hit
            continue
        try:
            pat = re.compile(re.escape(ident))
            hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if pat.search(k)), None)
        except re.error:
            hit = None
        out[ident] = hit if hit is not None else 'missing'
    return out


def main():
    results = load_results()
    f2p_res = match_idents(F2P, results)
    p2p_res = match_idents(P2P, results)

    f2p_pass   = [k for k, v in f2p_res.items() if v == 'pass']
    p2p_pass   = [k for k, v in p2p_res.items() if v == 'pass']

    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P), len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),
                           rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))

    print(json.dumps({
        'reward': reward,
        'f2p':    f2p_res,
        'p2p':    p2p_res,
        'f2p_pass_count': len(f2p_pass),
        'f2p_total':      len(F2P),
        'p2p_pass_count': len(p2p_pass),
        'p2p_total':      len(P2P),
    }, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
